title: TARP capital injection on bank risk-taking

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Difference-in-Differences (DID) with bank and time fixed effects (two-way fixed effects), supplemented by an event-study (dynamic DID) to test for parallel pre-trends and a robustness specification allowing for group-specific linear time trends.
- Why: TARP recipients self-selected. We leverage variation between treated (TARP) and control banks before vs. after TARP to identify the average treatment effect on the treated. With common treatment timing and balanced panel, TWFE is appropriate.
- Key identifying assumption: Parallel trends — in the absence of TARP, treated and control banks would have had the same evolution in non-performing loan (NPL) ratios. We assess this via:
  - Event-study lead coefficients (pre-period interactions) ≈ 0.
  - Pre-period differential trend test (treated × time trend in pre-periods) ≈ 0.
- Standard errors: Clustered at the bank (unit) level to account for serial correlation within banks.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Complete, self-contained R code
# - Reads the CSV file
# - Runs DID with bank and time FE
# - Reports the treatment effect and basic robustness checks

# Package setup -------------------------------------------------------------
req_pkgs <- c("data.table", "fixest")
to_install <- setdiff(req_pkgs, rownames(installed.packages()))
if(length(to_install)) install.packages(to_install, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
library(data.table)
library(fixest)

# Data ----------------------------------------------------------------------
path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s04_data.csv"
dt <- fread(path)

# Sanity checks
stopifnot(all(c("unit_id","period","treated","post","treat_x_post","y") %in% names(dt)))
# Ensure numeric period
dt[, period := as.integer(period)]
dt[, tnum := as.numeric(period)]  # helper linear time index

# MAIN DID: TWFE with bank and time FE -------------------------------------
mod_main <- feols(
  y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period,
  data = dt, cluster = ~ unit_id
)

# Extract and print main result
b <- coef(mod_main)["treat_x_post"]
ci <- confint(mod_main, "treat_x_post", level = 0.95)
se <- sqrt(vcov(mod_main)["treat_x_post","treat_x_post"])
pval <- 2 * (1 - pnorm(abs(b/se)))

cat("Main DID (TWFE) estimate for treat_x_post:\n")
cat(sprintf("  Coef = %0.6f, SE = %0.6f, 95%% CI = [%0.6f, %0.6f], p = %0.4f\n\n",
            b, se, ci[1], ci[2], pval))

# ROBUSTNESS 1: Allow treated group to have its own linear time trend -------
mod_trend <- feols(
  y ~ treat_x_post + treated:tnum | unit_id + period,
  data = dt, cluster = ~ unit_id
)
b_trend <- coef(mod_trend)["treat_x_post"]
se_trend <- sqrt(vcov(mod_trend)["treat_x_post","treat_x_post"])
ci_trend <- confint(mod_trend, "treat_x_post", level = 0.95)
pval_trend <- 2 * (1 - pnorm(abs(b_trend/se_trend)))

cat("Robustness: DID with group-specific linear trend (treated × time):\n")
cat(sprintf("  Coef = %0.6f, SE = %0.6f, 95%% CI = [%0.6f, %0.6f], p = %0.4f\n\n",
            b_trend, se_trend, ci_trend[1], ci_trend[2], pval_trend))

# PRE-TREND DIAGNOSTIC: pre-period differential trend only ------------------
pre_dt <- dt[post == 0]
mod_pretrend <- feols(
  y ~ treated:tnum | unit_id + period,
  data = pre_dt, cluster = ~ unit_id
)
b_pretrend <- coef(mod_pretrend)[1]
se_pretrend <- sqrt(vcov(mod_pretrend)[1,1])
pval_pretrend <- 2 * (1 - pnorm(abs(b_pretrend / se_pretrend)))

cat("Pre-period differential trend test (treated × time), using only pre-periods:\n")
cat(sprintf("  Coef = %0.6f, SE = %0.6f, p = %0.4f\n\n",
            b_pretrend, se_pretrend, pval_pretrend))

# EVENT STUDY: dynamic DID to assess pre-trends -----------------------------
# Use the last pre period as the reference period
base_period <- pre_dt[, max(period)]
mod_es <- feols(
  y ~ i(period, treated, ref = base_period) | unit_id + period,
  data = dt, cluster = ~ unit_id
)

es_coefs <- coef(mod_es)
es_names <- names(es_coefs)

# Identify pre-period interaction terms (period < base_period)
pre_periods <- sort(unique(pre_dt$period))
pre_periods <- pre_periods[pre_periods != base_period]
pre_terms <- paste0("period::", pre_periods, "#treated")
pre_terms <- pre_terms[pre_terms %in% es_names]

cat("Event-study pre-period coefficients (relative to last pre, period =", base_period, "):\n", sep="")
if(length(pre_terms) > 0){
  for(nm in pre_terms){
    cat(sprintf("  %s: %0.6f\n", nm, es_coefs[nm]))
  }
  # Joint test that all pre-period coefficients are zero
  cons <- paste0(pre_terms, " = 0", collapse = " & ")
  w <- wald(mod_es, cons)
  cat(sprintf("  Joint test (all pre-period effects = 0): F = %0.3f, df1 = %d, p = %0.4f\n\n",
              w$stat, w$df1, w$p.value))
} else {
  cat("  No identified pre-period interactions (check input data).\n\n")
}

# SIMPLE SANITY CHECK: group means DiD --------------------------------------
agg <- dt[, .(
  y_mean = mean(y, na.rm=TRUE)
), by = .(treated, post)]
wide <- dcast(agg, treated ~ post, value.var = "y_mean")
setnames(wide, c("treated","pre","post"))
if(all(c("0","1") %in% names(dcast(agg, treated ~ post, value.var = "y_mean")))){
  # Print only if both groups exist
  cat("Simple (unadjusted) DiD on means (post - pre treated) - (post - pre control):\n")
  agg_means <- dt[, .(y = mean(y)), by = .(treated, post)]
  pre_t <- agg_means[treated==1 & post==0, y]
  post_t <- agg_means[treated==1 & post==1, y]
  pre_c <- agg_means[treated==0 & post==0, y]
  post_c <- agg_means[treated==0 & post==1, y]
  did_simple <- (post_t - pre_t) - (post_c - pre_c)
  cat(sprintf("  Unadjusted DiD = %0.6f\n", did_simple))
}

# Final echo of main causal parameter ---------------------------------------
cat("\nFinal causal estimate (preferred TWFE):\n")
cat(sprintf("  TARP effect on NPL ratio (treat × post) = %0.6f\n", b))
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Positive. If capital support relaxed constraints and induced moral hazard, TARP recipients likely expanded risk-taking at the margin, leading to higher subsequent NPL ratios relative to controls.
- Magnitude: Modest but economically meaningful. I expect an increase on the order of 0.10–0.30 percentage points in the NPL ratio (10–30 bps) for treated banks relative to controls in the post period, after netting out common shocks. The exact magnitude depends on sample composition and timing, but a small positive DID estimate is plausible given the crisis backdrop.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: DID — treated=TARP recipients, control=non-recipients; parallel pre-trends required
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: TARP banks show higher NPL ratios post-injection, consistent with moral hazard
_ground_truth.main_effect: 20bp increase in NPL ratio for TARP banks
